name: Bergbau- und Salzwelten Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: The Salzwelten and Mining Museum in Hall in Tirol: A reconstructed salt mine gallery in the historic old town with shafts, tools, and salt history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Mining Museum and Salzwelten Hall in Tirol are nestled in the heart of the medieval old town of Hall in Tirol (Hall-Wattens region) at an altitude of approximately 574 meters. "White gold" shaped the town of Hall for centuries like no other industry: following the discovery of rich rock salt deposits in the Halltal valley in the 13th century, Hall developed into the region's preeminent salt metropolis. Inside the historic Fürstengebäude at Fürstengasse 1, dedicated miners and historians created a unique underground museum that brings the enigmatic world of the Halltal salt chambers right into the city, making it one of the region's most captivating destinations.

Route & Requirements

The centerpiece of the museum is the faithfully reconstructed salt mine gallery in the vaulted cellar of the Fürstengebäude: with authentic timber framing, narrow windlass passages, shafts, and a genuine wooden miners' slide, the exhibition conveys the authentic atmosphere of historical high-mountain salt extraction. Highlights include antique pit lamps, chisels, blasting tools, and drilling machinery spanning various centuries, as well as detailed relief models of the enormous leaching caverns in the Halltal. Engaging display boards and listening stations illustrate the arduous and perilous labor of the miners, the engineering of the historic wooden brine pipeline to the saline in Hall, and the town's economic heyday as a premier Alpine trading hub and mint. For children and families, donning a helmet and mine lamp for the underground tour is a thrilling adventure.

Visit & Arrival

The Mining Museum and Salzwelten Hall are open from May to October on Saturdays from 10:00 to 16:00, and year-round as part of guided city and gallery tours organized by the tourist board (advance booking at the Hall tourist office). Admission fees (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths approx. €3.50, children under 6 free. Getting there: The Fürstengebäude is located centrally in Hall's old town (Fürstengasse 1), a short stroll from the upper town square and Hasegg Castle. By public transport: S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 depart Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof every 15 minutes to Hall in Tirol (travel time approx. 9 minutes), followed by a seven-minute walk to the historic center. Motorists can use the Altstadtgarage Hall or the Untere Stadt parking garage.

Tips

The underground gallery maintains a cool, constant temperature year-round—a light jacket and sturdy walking shoes are highly recommended for the tour. Combine your trip to the salt world with a visit to nearby Hasegg Castle and its iconic Mint Tower, followed by a leisurely stroll through the heritage-listed alleyways of Tyrol's largest medieval old town.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Okt Sa 10:00–16:00 Uhr sowie ganzjährig im Rahmen geführter Touren
